chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a newborn who has neither what belongs to males nor what belongs to females. He said:

For this one, the Imam conducts a lot-drawing. He writes on one lot: ʿAbdullāh, and on another lot: Amatullāh. Then the Imam, or the one drawing the lot, says: O Allah, You are Allah, there is no god but You...
Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that wherein they used to differ.
Make clear to us the matter of this newborn, so that he may inherit what You have ordained for him in Your Book.
Then he places the two lots among unspecified lots, then they are mixed; whichever of the two comes out, inheritance is assigned according to it.

key_terms.أَمَةُ اللَّهِ: the female designation written on another lot
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam who oversees and executes the procedure
key_terms.سَهْمٍ: a marked lot or slip used in the draw
key_terms.عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ: Knower of the unseen and the seen, invoking Allah’s complete knowledge
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: the male designation written on one lot
key_terms.يُقْرَعُ: lots are drawn to determine the ruling

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined in a hadith for a newborn whose sex is unclear?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for determining the inheritance status of a newborn whose sex is not outwardly distinguishable. It describes the Imam عليه السلام using qurʿah (lot-drawing) together with du'a to seek Allah’s judgment so that inheritance may be distributed according to what Allah has prescribed in His Book.
